matches.context: Montenegro have won Group C2 with a game to spare. They have 13 points from five games (four wins and a draw, 9-5) after beating Latvia 2-1 at home on 12 November, so Cyprus (maximum 11) can no longer catch them, and they go up to League B. Cyprus are second on 8 (2W 2D 1L, 6-4), the promotion play-off place, after a 1-1 draw in Armenia on 12 November (Pikis 9', Gharibyan 58'). Armenia, on 5, can only draw level if they beat Latvia and Cyprus lose. Cyprus would still finish second on head-to-head, having beaten Armenia 2-0 at home on 2 October and drawn in Yerevan. Based on the table, neither side's final position looks likely to change. Montenegro won the reverse fixture 2-1 at home on 25 September. This is both teams' last Nations League game of the campaign.

matches.context: Group C2 after five games: Montenegro 13 pts (9-5), Cyprus 8 (6-4), Armenia 5 (5-6), Latvia 1 (3-8) (FotMob). The final placings look settled, so this is effectively a dead rubber. Montenegro have won the group. Latvia cannot climb off the bottom (4 points maximum). Armenia can at most draw level with Cyprus on 8, and Cyprus would finish ahead on head-to-head after beating them 2-0 in Nicosia and drawing 1-1 in Yerevan (our inference from the results; UEFA's first tie-breaker is head-to-head). Armenia won the reverse fixture 2-0 in Yerevan on 25 September. Matchday 5 (12 Nov): Montenegro 2-1 Latvia (Krstović 70', Meļņiks 72', Maraš 90+1') and Armenia 1-1 Cyprus (Pikis 9', Gharibyan 58'). Latvia have not won in this campaign (1 draw, 4 defeats) and have not scored more than once in any of their last eight Nations League games (KickOff). Armenia have drawn their last two (0-0 in Montenegro, 1-1 v Cyprus), but their away form in competitive games is L-L-L-L-D (22Bet/API-Football). Latvia stayed in League C last March by beating Gibraltar in a relegation play-off (Sports Mole). No source we found says what fourth place means in this edition.

matches.context: Decider for top spot in Group C1. Albania lead with 12 points (W4 L1, 10-3) and Belarus are second on 10 (W3 D1 L1, 7-2); Finland have 7 and San Marino 0, so only these two can win the group. A draw is enough for Albania to finish first and win promotion to League B, while Belarus must win. Belarus are already sure of at least second: Finland can only reach 10 points, and Belarus lead the head-to-head (0-0 away, 1-0 at home). Albania won the reverse fixture 2-0 in Tirana on 26 September. Matchday 5 (12 Nov): Albania 2-0 Finland (Muçi 35', Manaj 50'; Finland's Tehno sent off 67') and San Marino 0-2 Belarus (Gomanov 12', Kontsevoy 17'). Belarus have won three and drawn one of their four games since Tirana, without conceding. Belarus play their 'home' games on neutral ground abroad, and this one is in Budapest at Vasas's Illovszky Rudolf Stadion, which holds about 5,000. Kick-off is 17:00 GMT (18:00 CET).

news.text: No Belarus injuries reported. Viktor Goncharenko's side are unbeaten in four and kept four clean sheets in five Nations League games, but they commit 18.4 fouls a game (second-most in the competition).
Belarus need a win to overtake Albania and top the group. A draw or defeat leaves them second, and Finland cannot catch them on head-to-head.
Goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha is injured. Armando Broja, Anis Mehmeti and Marash Kumbulla were not selected for the November squad, and Dinamo City right-back Ysni Ismaili got a first call-up.

Rolando Maran is expected to keep the XI that beat Finland 2-0 on Thursday. Etrit Berisha is back in goal after serving his ban for the October red card, and Ylber Ramadani was booked against Finland.
Albania need only a draw to win the group and promotion to League B. Albanian media say they can 'play for two results'.

Matanović leads the line instead of Beljo in the statz.ai, Mr Fixit's Tips and Khel Now XIs. The statz.ai XI is a 3-4-2-1 (Smolčić, Mišić, Vlašić, Sučić, Matanović), and both it and Mr Fixit's Tips were published before Vlašić was left out of the squad and Sučić fell ill. news.text: Nikola Vlašić is not on the 23-man list submitted to UEFA, and no official reason has been given. He played 90 minutes at left-back at Wembley.

Sučić is out with a virus and high fever. Bilić said he is 'better, but… won't be able to play tomorrow'. Svijet Kladjenja names Petar Sučić, who scored the Wembley equaliser, and statz.ai and KickOff credit Petar with Croatia's Nations League goal. Sportnet, Khel Now and Fotbalzprávy name Luka, and Sportnet's 23-man list includes Petar but not Luka.
Ivan Perišić returns from the suspension that ruled him out at Wembley and is expected to start on the left. Luka Modrić is expected to start.
Josip Šutalo, Marin Pongračić (thigh) and Kristijan Jakić (knee) are injured, and Andrej Kramarić is not in the squad.

news.text: Baturina, Vlašić, Matanović and Sučić did a reduced session in Friday's training. Seven players have one yellow card: Modrić, Kovačić, Vušković, Smolčić, Mišić, Pašalić and Sučić.

A defeat would relegate Croatia from League A, and even a win only secures third place and a March play-off, after Germany beat Serbia 3-1. Croatia have lost four in a row, including 0-7 at home to England.

Captain Ladislav Krejčí is suspended after his second red card of the campaign, at 72' against Spain at Letná. Czechia have had three reds in five games (Šulc against England, and Krejčí twice). He has travelled with the squad.
Lukáš Provod, Štěpán Chaloupek and Martin Šubert have left the squad, Provod and Chaloupek through illness. Filip Prebsl (Plzeň) and Matěj Jurásek (Sparta) were called up.
Robin Hranáč is missing (Fotbalzprávy). Mr Fixit's Tips also lists Pavel Šulc, Adam Karabec and Ondřej Lingr as injured.
Michal Sadílek is available again after a yellow-card ban, and Tomáš Souček, back from an ankle-ligament injury, is expected to start.
Czechia have lost all five group games (2-12), managed only 1.2 shots on target a game and have never beaten Croatia. Any win would take them to third and a March play-off.

matches.context: Both teams are already through to the quarter-finals, so this game decides first place in Group A3. Spain top the group with 15 points from five wins (14-5). England are second on 12 (16-4), Croatia have 3 and Czechia 0. Spain won the reverse fixture 3-2 at Wembley on 26 September, so a draw or a Spain win keeps them first. An England win would draw them level on 15 points. On UEFA's usual tie-breakers, England would then go top with any win: a two-goal margin wins the head-to-head, and after a one-goal win the head-to-head is level and England have the better overall goal difference (+12 against +9 now). Matchday 5 on 12 November: Czechia 0-2 Spain and England 2-1 Croatia. Spain have won 12 in a row and are unbeaten in 43 games since March 2024, not counting shoot-outs (22Bet). England's only defeat in the group was the 3-2 loss to Spain.

news.text: Lamine Yamal missed the 2-0 win in Prague with slight knee inflammation and stayed in Barcelona. He was expected to be fit for Sunday and to rejoin the squad on Thursday night or Friday, giving him two training sessions. 22Bet expects him to start.

Mikel Oyarzabal, Spain's top scorer in 2026 with 9 goals, missed Prague with flu and is waiting for the birth of his second child. De la Fuente said Spain would wait until the last moment. 22Bet expects him back. Víctor Muñoz was called up as cover.
Rodri is injured, and Dani Olmo and Eric García are not in the squad.
Martín Zubimendi plays in a protective mask after breaking his nose. 22Bet expects Pedri to return to midfield after he did not start in Prague.
Marc Guéhi withdrew injured on 9 Nov, and Dan Burn was called up in his place. Bukayo Saka and Marcus Rashford are also out injured. Cole Palmer, Phil Foden and Kobbie Mainoo were not selected.
Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence both missed the Croatia game. Tuchel hoped they could train on their own on Friday, rejoin the squad on Saturday and be available on Sunday.
Harry Kane became England's most-capped player (126) against Croatia. Bournemouth's James Hill got his first senior call-up. England need a win to take top spot.
